sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This bulbous lily of western North America grows in open forests, clearings, thickets and meadows, from southern British Columbia to northern California and Idaho. Its stem is about 40–120 cm tall; the white scaly bulb is 3–5 cm across.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The lance-shaped leaves, often in whorls of 6–9, are about 4–10 cm long. The pendent, spotted orange to red-orange flowers have strongly recurved tepals 4–6 cm long. The upright capsule is 3–5 cm long.

sections.title: Uses and cautions
sections.text: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest have eaten the bulbs after various preparations. This is not a foraging recommendation. Like other true lilies, the plant can cause severe kidney poisoning in cats.
